novel_features.name: Time-windowed top workflows
novel_features.description: Rank the highest-upvoted workflows inside a time window like 7d or 30d.
novel_features.rationale: The community API exposes sort=top but has no date filter at all, so 'best rated this week' is impossible against the live endpoint; it only works by mirroring posts locally and windowing on createdAt.
novel_features.why_it_matters: This is the answer to 'bring me the best workflows this week' in one call instead of paging the feed and eyeballing dates.

novel_features.name: Use-case finder
novel_features.description: Answer 'are there any workflows for X' by blending the server's semantic search with local full-text search, then ranking by upvotes.
novel_features.rationale: Neither search alone is enough: the server's q= is semantic but returns unranked slices, and local FTS is exact but misses conceptual matches. Merging and de-duplicating the two requires a local mirror.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever someone asks whether the community has already solved a problem, before designing a workflow from scratch.

novel_features.name: Full workflow reader
novel_features.description: Print one workflow in full - body, tools, industries, author and comments - in a single call.
novel_features.rationale: The API has no single-post endpoint; fetching one workflow with its discussion means combining a filtered list call with a separate comments call and reassembling them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this after search to actually read a workflow instead of returning a truncated feed card.

novel_features.name: Community digest
novel_features.description: Summarise a time window: how many workflows landed, the top posts, the most-used tools and the busiest authors.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating every post in the window across four dimensions at once; the feed endpoint returns one page of raw cards with no rollups.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for a standing 'what happened in the community' check rather than scrolling the feed.

novel_features.name: Tool adoption ranking
novel_features.description: Rank AI tools by how often they appear in workflows and by the upvotes those workflows earned.
novel_features.rationale: The tools endpoint returns a flat catalogue with no usage data whatsoever; adoption counts only exist by joining every mirrored post against its tool tags locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to see which tools the community actually builds with, as opposed to which ones merely exist in the dropdown.

novel_features.name: Tool co-occurrence stacks
novel_features.description: Show which other tools appear alongside a given tool, so you can see the stacks people really run.
novel_features.rationale: A self-join across the mirrored post-to-tool mapping. There is no API surface for tool relationships of any kind.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when picking complementary tooling, or to answer 'what do people pair with X'.

narrative.headline: Search the community's AI workflows offline, and rank them by week - two things the site's own API cannot do.
narrative.value_prop: The Rundown's community feed has no date filter and no single-post endpoint, so questions like 'best rated this week' or 'read me that whole workflow' need a local mirror. This CLI syncs every workflow into SQLite, then answers them instantly with `top --since`, `use-cases`, `show`, `digest`, `tools rank` and `stack`. No account or API key is needed - every read endpoint is public.
narrative.auth_narrative: No authentication required. Every read endpoint used by this CLI (`/posts`, `/posts/{id}/comments`, `/tools`, `/leaderboard`) is served publicly without a session. Upvoting, bookmarking, commenting and posting do require a signed-in Clerk session and are deliberately not implemented here.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the community API is reachable - no key or login needed
Mirror every workflow into local SQLite; everything below is then offline and instant
The best-rated workflows from the last week
Ask whether the community has already solved a problem
A rollup of what landed this week and which tools drove it

troubleshoots.fix: Run `rundown-pp-cli sync` first - these commands read the local mirror, not the live API.
The server caps page size at 50. Use `sync` plus the local commands when you need the whole corpus.
Pass the slug, not the display name. Run `rundown-pp-cli tools` for valid tool slugs.
Known upstream behaviour - the API ignores the period parameter and always returns the weekly window.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever a question is about AI workflows the Rundown community has shared: whether a use case already exists, what the highest-rated recent posts are, which tools people actually build with, or what a specific workflow says end to end. It is the fast path for all of those - the whole corpus is mirrored locally, so answers come back without browsing the site.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to upvote, bookmark, comment on, or publish posts - those need a signed-in session and are not implemented.
Do not use it for The Rundown's newsletter archive or news articles; it only covers the community workflow hub.
Do not use it as a general AI-tool directory - `tools` reflects only what this community has tagged.

recipes.title: Best workflows this week
recipes.explanation: Windows the local mirror by createdAt and ranks by upvotes - the query the live API cannot express.

recipes.title: Does a use case exist for this?
recipes.explanation: Runs the server's semantic search and local FTS together, de-duplicates, and ranks what comes back by upvotes.

recipes.title: Narrow to one tool and read the winners
recipes.explanation: Server-side tool filtering with a trimmed agent payload - only three fields come back instead of full post bodies.

recipes.title: What do people pair with n8n?
recipes.explanation: Self-joins the mirrored post-to-tool mapping to surface the stacks that co-occur in real workflows.

recipes.title: Read one workflow end to end
recipes.explanation: Reassembles the post and its comment thread into a single readable document, body included in full.
